industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the United States consumer surveys fell again (University of Michigan 46.3 preliminary October, down 1.8; Conference Board 81.9 in September, down 6.7; Goldman Sachs 19 Oct), consumer discretionary lagged with technology and communication services in the week's rotation (Jefferies, 17 Oct), and the European consumer was again not read, so the row rests on the US reading and on the regime. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, D prior, the largest industry in the universe at 138 stocks. Counter-case: Retail physical reads B and Online retail A on relative strength, Hotels C, which is where cheap good businesses accumulate, and a double notch on 138 stocks shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists; the exceptions are carried at sector level (H.3 Neutral).

sector.why: Underweight. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): discretionary spend and complex regulatory cases. Relative strength AGREES, F both readings. Counter-case: gambling spend has historically been resilient in downturns.

geography.why: Neutral, from Overweight. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): the condition written on this row on 2-Oct-26 (it stays B only while the Banks row is Overweight) is no longer met, since Banks goes to Neutral on the credit tripwire; the Greek listings in the MI Pool are six banks plus Cenergy, HELLENiQ Energy and Motor Oil, with the live holding Ballys Intralot beside them, so the country letter was a second bank weight, and in a week when European sovereign stress is spreading from France to Italy and Spain a bank-heavy periphery listing is where contagion lands next, though Greek spreads themselves were not read. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case: Goldman Sachs's emerging market team (8 Oct) stays overweight Greece by name, Greece is not among the sovereigns named under stress, and the Greek energy names are on the right side of the regime; back to B if the Banks row returns to Overweight.
